findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

On arrival the PIC was unable to provide a vomit/diarrheal event clean up kit or procedures. They normally have a body fluid kit sufficient for this issue available but were unable to find/produce it during this inspection. A procedure was given during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that the procedures/kit is available at al times in the facility.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Sandwich containers were observed with the food contact surfaces up/exposed on top of the prep line shelving. The situation was discussed with the PIC and managers and the items were flipped over to correct. Ensure that all single service food contact surfaces are protected from contamination at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Two locations in the facility were discussed with the PIC as having damaged floor tiles and grouting that was accumulating food residues. These locations are near the drive thru area and should be repaired prior to the next routine inspection. Maintain the facility in a smooth and easily cleanable state.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

A large accumulation of ice was observed on the floor in the active walk in freezer. This posses a cleaning concern and was discussed with the PIC during the inspection. They were instructed to clean/remove the ice and maintain it clean moving forward. Ensure that all floors are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

Multiple employees were observed throughout the inspection to wash their hands and then turn off the faucet with their bare hands. The PIC was notified and instructed to review hand washing procedures with all staff and monitor hand washing moving forward in order to promote safe practices.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:

The metal sheet wall to the right of the fryers is observed pulling away from the wall and exposing a gap that is not easily cleanable. There are also pieces of cardboard and a cloth rag in parts of this gap holding it apart. The location was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to repair the wall and ensure a smooth and easily cleanable surface. Repair this location prior to the next routine inspection and ensure that all facilities are maintained in a smooth and easily cleanable state.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(8) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge including section 1-17).

The PIC was not showing active managerial control in relation to the cold holding situation related to the walk in cooler (refer to line item number 22). The PIC was aware of an issue and maintained use of a failing cold holding unit, even allowing for new product to be put into the cooler after admitting to knowing that it was not functioning correctly. The managerial staff is also having ongoing issues with CFPM certificates. One was available at the end of today’s inspection, but was not here when the inspection began. Having all managerial staff with this certification would ensure that food safety concerns are understood at all times. Education was conducted and possible procedures for future situations were discussed with the PIC during this inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available in the facility. Mrs. McLemore arrived during this inspection to correct. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts/all times that foods are being handled or prepared. She stated that the CFPM that should have been there was having car trouble and she was needed to acquire stock from another store due to discarding the items from the walk in cooler (refer to line item number 22).

Inside of the ice machine is a piece hanging down behind the defector shield. Today it is observed with possible rust residue. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain this equipment clean moving forward. The items was cleaned during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Multiple TCS items in the walk in cooler are observed with internal temperatures between 48F-50F. The PIC was told and stated that they knew the cooler was having issues at 9 am this morning. They put in a work order at that time. Several of the TCS foods were prepared today, but were placed into the cooler to long ago (per the PIC) for them to be safe at these temperatures. The foods are all observed with internal temperatures within the range of the coolers ambient temperature. All of these items were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Items discarded include sliced tomatoes (7 quarter pans), mayonnaise (out of the package and portioned) (5 quarter pans), diced/cooked chicken (3 quarter pans), maple honey butter (labeled as refrigerate after thawing) (three containers), chopped lettuce (one large tub, six cases), 16 premade salads and multiple cheeses. Two containers of beef were placed into the cooler approximately an hour prior to observation. These were allowed to be moved to a correctly functioning cooler and saved. Ensure that all TCS foods are maintained at effective temperatures at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

Multiple items in the walk in the walk in cooler appear to be incorrectly date marked. Per the employee the items (chopped lettuce, sliced tomatoes and sliced onions) were all prepared this morning. These items are all showing preparation dates ranging over the past three days. The PIC was shown and instructed to review and re-educate use of the label maker for future items. These items were discarded due to temperature abuse during this inspection (refer to line item #22).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The walk in cooler in the facility is not effectively holding foods at safe temperatures (refer to line item number 22). The maintenance tech arrived during this inspection to fix it. Per him, stop leak was added to the system and then more Freon was added. By the end of the inspection the cooler is observed at effective cold holding temperatures. Ensure that all coolers are maintained in effective states at all times.

The three part sink in the dish area is observed with a leak coming from the faucet. The PIC was shown and stated that a work order had already been put in and the maintenance person was scheduled to be at the facility today. He arrived and ordered a part for overnight delivery. This is confirmed via messages noted on the closing manager’s phone with the district manager. A follow up is being set for Friday to ensure that the repair is completed.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Multiple pans and utensils stored for use in the dish area of the facility are observed with food debris remaining on them. findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The B side of the prep line does not appear to have been cleaned when shut down 1-1.5 weeks ago. The PIC was shown and removed the drawers to begin immediate cleaning. Ensure that all food debris is removed from the food areas regularly to prevent accumulation and potential contamination in the future. This will also help prevent possible pests issues in the future.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

A McFlurry is observed in the standing freezer at the back of the facility stored alongside other foods intended for consumers. The PIC was shown and discarded the ice cream to correct. There are areas designated for employee foods in the facility that should be being used. Ensure that the designated (and separated) areas are used moving forward.

findings.comment:
1) Frosty mix in the standing cooler next to the ice machine was at 65F. 2) The cooler under the lemonade had half-and-half creamer which was also at 65F. The PIC was consulted and voluntarily threw out the items which were out of temperature during this inspection. Educated the importance of keeping food out of the temperature danger zone. The PIC said they would ensure the cooler is repaired and functioning correctly (see line 33).

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed cooked/cooled beef in the walk-in cooler that did not have date marking. Discussed with PIC and they were not sure when the meat was made, so it was discarded. Ensure that food held for more than 24 hours is clearly marked to ensure that it is not held for longer than 7 days.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed the standing cooler next to the ice machine was holding foods from 64-67F. PICs were consulted and food was discarded (refer to line 22). Follow-up in 10 days to ensure the cooler is repaired and functioning correctly.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Observed the hanging thermometer in the walk-in cooler and a standing freezer-freezer were reading significantly lower temperatures than the actual temperature of the coolers. Ensure that thermometers are accurate to +/- 3F.  The inspector will follow-up on 06/27/2024 to ensure there are accurate thermometers in the coolers.

4-203.12: (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be accurate to +/- 1.5C. (B) accurate to +/- 3 Fahrenheit.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed the lid of the ice machine had a small amount of a brown/tan substance smeared on a small part of the inside of the lid. The PIC cleaned off the substance with a sanitizer rag. Ensure that food is protected from contamination in the ice machine.

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed single-use cups being stored inside a cardboard box on the floor. Ensure that single-use articles are stored at least 6-inches above the floor to protect against contamination.

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed several non-food contact surfaces having an accumulation of soil residues: (1) The tray and gaps in the shelving trays underneath the fries hot-holding; (2) Behind the trays of chicken nuggets hot-holding; (3) The drawers and above the drawers in the B side. Ensure that these non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid soil accumulation.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed several physical facilities which need to be cleaned: (1) Mold on stickers in the walk-in cooler; (2) Mold on shelving in the walk-in cooler; (3) mold on the light fixture in the walk-in cooler; (4) Soil under the CO2 container; (5) Frost in the standing freezer next to the fryers; (6) Soil behind the purple-colored frosty machine; (7) food splash on the counter next to the chili hot holding. Ensure that all physical facilities are cleaned as necessary to keep than clean.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed drains under the 2-part sink and 3-part sink did not have covers. Ensure covers are provided.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
(1) Observed a backpack that was hanging above food and clean equipment. The backpack was moved into an employee storage area. Ensure that employees are always storing their personal items in the designated employee area. (2) Observed a personal cake parfait stored in the walk-in cooler amongst foods intended for consumers. The cake parfait was thrown away by the PIC. Ensure that employees food and drinks are stored below and away from food attended for consumers.

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival none of the buckets or the three part sink would register on the inspector's or facility’s sanitizer test strips. Investigation led to the belief that the line was dirty and not allowing the proper amount of concentrate to reach the dispenser. The line was cleaned by employees. This allowed the machine to function correctly and the buckets/sink in the facility were remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

1) Boxes of food are observed on the floor in the walk in freezer; 2) a box of food is observed on the floor in the walk in cooler; 3) boxes of fries are observed on the floor in the fry walk in cooler. The items were all moved during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored safely or off the floor.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Multiple employees are observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that hand washing takes place prior to gloves use.

findings.comment:

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani buckets along the prep line do not register quat sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. The buckets were remade during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

PIC indicated that this location has not been used for a couple months. Foods were discarded and the drawers cleaned during the insepction to correct the violation.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). The door to the walk in cooler storing predominately bread and fries has a crack running along the cooler side of the door and is pulling away from the rest of the door. This is exposing the inner insulation and needs to be repaired. Repair prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Observed employee wash hands then turn faucet off without the use of a barrier/paper towel to prevent recontamination of clean hands. CORRECTED- Provided education and discussed with PIC.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Employee observed filling a beverage cup at the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and provided education.
5-205.11: (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs observed stored above lettuce in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Cooler rearranged to prevent cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Salads in the cookline prep cooler (bottom) observed at 75F. Technicians responded during inspection and got the cooler temperature dropping, but complete repairs will be completed by next Friday. Items on the top of the cooler are already tracked with Time as a Control. Until cooler is functioning properly, no TCS foods may be stored in the cooler. Salads were moved to the functioning cooler to rapidly cool to 41F or below. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Thermometers in the vertical dressing cooler and the vertical cookline freezer observed to be damaged. Ensure functional thermometers are present in all cold holding units.
4-204.112: (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Employees observed using cups to scoop ice at the drive thru. Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff use ice scoop rather than cups to scoop ice.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee wash hands then turn faucet off without the use of a barrier/paper towel to prevent recontamination of clean hands. CORRECTED— Provided education and discussed with PIC.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels provided at the handsink near the ice machine. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC, who provided paper towels.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
Chicken nuggets observed held without indicating the time they were prepared or when they would be discarded. Discussion with PIC indicated that they are held using time as a control. CORRECTED— Nuggets were still hot and allowed to be kept. Facility uses timers to keep track of discard times and the appropriate timer was set for the Wendy’s-established time for chicken nuggets (30 minutes).
3-501.19: (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. [P]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Employees observed using cups to scoop ice at the drive thru. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff use ice scoop rather than cups to scoop ice.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: No sanitizer bucket present at time of inspection. Employee filled sanitizer buckets to appropriate concentration. CORRECTED— PIC and another employee adjusted dispenser. Sanitizer registered at 200ppm quat.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee enter kitchen with gloves on and begin working. CORRECTED— Provided education. Employee returned to handwashing sink, removed gloves and washed hands before returning to work.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No soap provided at front handwashing sink. CORRECTED— Soap dispenser was refilled. Ensure soap is always provided at handwashing sinks.
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Sanitizer bucket on the prep line had no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- Sanitizer registered at 200ppm quat.
4-501.114: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration of 200-400 ppm or as specified by the manufacturer's label. [Pf]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Knife observed stored in the gap between a knife rack and the wall. CORRECTED— Knife removed to be washed, rinsed and sanitized prior to storage in a clean location.
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: No sanitizer bucket present at time of inspection. Employee filled sanitizer buckets, which did not register on inspector’s test strips. CORRECTED— PIC and another employee adjusted dispenser. Sanitizer registered at 200ppm quat.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment: PIC was unaware of any written clean up policy for vomit/diarrhea. CORRECTED-- Inspector provided a written policy. Keep available in case clean up is needed. Ref.2-501.11  [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Facility is not under the supervision of a certified food protection manager. Ensure sufficient staff are certified food managers to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
PIC could not provide a written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy to be reviewed during inspection. A written policy (or a kit) must be available at all times for reference if/when needed.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket on the prep line had no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC and remade sanitizer to correct concentration.
4-501.114: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration of 200-400 ppm or as specified by the manufacturer's label. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Drive-thru ice bin left exposed/open when not in use. Keep ice bin covered when not in use to protect ice from contamination. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC. Ice bin closed.
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Several small containers of milk are 50°F in the low cooler near the cash registers. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment: Observed employee refilling bacon container on prep line with bare hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and provided education. Bacon will be discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11 (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in ¶¶ (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. (P)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed no concentration quat sanitizer in buckets and at 3 compartment sink (from dispenser). CORRECTED- PIC was able to adjust dispenser to dispense at the proper concentration. Dishes need to be re-sanitized and buckets need to be refilled.
4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. (P)

Observed small accumulation of pink slime in ice machine. Service as often as necessary to maintain clean to sight and touch. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Ice machine will be cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 (B) (1) (C) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Cloths used for wping counters in the kitchen area were observed stored in solutions of Quat the triggered a small color change on the inspectors test strips (approximately 50 ppm). Quat sanitizers should be between 200-400 ppm. The PIC adjusted the machine and new buckets were made at 400 ppm Quat.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 (Pf) A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

When asked, the facility could only provide test strips intended for chlorine (CL) based sanitizers. The sanitizers in the facility use a Quat based sanitizer. DIscussed with the PIC and instructed to aquire test strips intended for Quat sanitizers.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 (C) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

The mop sink in the rear of the kitchen area was observed with a side that was heavily chipped. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to repair or replace prior to the nextt routine inspection.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment: Facility without hot water. Repair or Replace water heater.
